u0: The shop is in a clean state: the siren is silent, every client who arrived has been served, and no dropped food needs an immediate pickup. There is no single completion milestone; the shop simply has to keep running correctly as new events arrive. The agent is free to reposition or wait, but a new ring will demand the switch, a new client will demand service, and a new slip will demand that food be back in hand on the very next step.
u1: The siren is ringing and has not been silenced, so the outstanding job is to reach the switch and turn it off; no client is waiting unserved and no dropped food needs an immediate pickup. The siren stays on until it is switched off, so there is nothing to wait for. Toggling the switch clears the duty and returns the shop to a clean state, unless a client arrives or food slips along the way and adds a new obligation.
u2: A slip has just occurred and no other duty is pending, so the only requirement is that food be in hand again on the very next step. The agent must use this single step to recover the dropped portion, normally by picking it up immediately, or the task fails for good. The recovery cannot be postponed to a later step.
u3: The siren is ringing and food has just slipped, so two duties are open at once. The food must be back in hand on the very next step or the task fails for good; silencing the siren does not remove that requirement. After the food is secured, the siren still has to be switched off.
u4: A client is waiting and has not been served; the siren is silent and no dropped food needs an immediate pickup. The order may already be taken and the food prepared, but the duty is cleared only by serving the client; taking the order or preparing food alone leaves it open. If the siren starts or food slips before the handoff, that new obligation is added on top.
u5: A client is waiting to be served while the siren is ringing, so two duties are open together. They can be handled in either order or interleaved: silencing the siren clears only the siren duty, and serving the client clears only the client duty. Both must eventually be completed, and a food slip in the meantime would add a one-step recovery demand.
u6: A client is waiting to be served, and food has just slipped. The agent has one step to be holding food again or the task fails for good, while the client's service is still owed afterwards. Serving is the only thing that clears the client duty, and the slip recovery cannot be postponed.
u7: All three duties are open at once: a client is waiting to be served, the siren is ringing, and food has just slipped. The food must be in hand again on the very next step or the task fails permanently, regardless of what else is happening. After the slip is recovered, the client's service and silencing the siren remain, and those two can be done in either order.
u8: Reaching this state means the immediate-recovery rule has been broken for good: after food slipped, the very next step ended without food in the agent's hands. That mandatory requirement can no longer be satisfied, so the task has failed and successful completion is impossible. No later pickup, service, or switch toggle can repair it.
